seo.title: Friends at Casa Club · Kibay at Ocoa Bay
seo.description: Bring your people to Casa Club: a long table facing the bay, glasses poured without rush, and unpretentious Caribbean cooking. The honest way to spend Saturday at Ocoa Bay.

hero.eyebrow: Reason #2 · A Way to Enjoy Kibay
hero.title: Your people, Casa Club, no rush
hero.lead: A long table, glasses that don't stay empty, conversation that runs long. Casa Club at Ocoa Bay was built to let Saturday last as long as it needs to.
hero.imageAlt: Friends at Ocoa Bay's Casa Club toasting with Kibay overlooking the bay

story.heading: The good thing about a long table
story.p1: You arrive with the kind of people you can sit quiet with. Casa Club has that thing few places in the Dominican Republic have: it welcomes you without protocol. You sit down, you look at the bay, someone orders the first bottle of Kibay, and the afternoon doesn't need much more to begin.
story.p2: The menu is honest — farm-to-table Caribbean cooking, whatever the kitchen is doing well that day, whatever came in fresh from the property. A ceviche, some cheeses, a shared main. Glasses are poured slowly, the sparkling stays cold, the sun goes down without you noticing.
story.p3: This isn't an Instagram brunch. It's a table with your people, in a Caribbean vineyard, with wines made two hours from Santo Domingo. By the time you look up, you're already planning the next Saturday.

experiences.heading: Experiences at Ocoa Bay
experiences.subheading: Book your day at the Caribbean's working vineyard — tour, tasting, and farm-to-table dining.

closing.heading: Want a different way to enjoy Kibay?
closing.body: Five reasons to open a bottle at Ocoa Bay. This is just one of them.
